comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance includes qualitative reserves for losses expected but not adequately reflected in quantitative methods, considering factors such as changes in lending policies, business conditions, portfolio concentrations, past due loans, external factors, and model uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Bank of America (BAC) disclose the inclusion and purpose of qualitative reserves (or adjustments) within their Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) to cover risks not fully captured by quantitative models. Citi specifically highlights a year-over-year decline in its qualitative component driven by the release of pandemic-related uncertainty reserves, whereas BAC's disclosure focuses on the static methodology and factors considered (such as lending policy changes and model uncertainty) without detailing a year-over-year quantitative shift in the qualitative component in this specific text.

sentences.text: Citi's qualitative component declined year-over-year, primarily driven by (i) the full release of COVID-19-related uncertainty reserves, as the portfolio delinquencies and losses have increased and these risks are now captured in the quantitative component of the ACL, and (ii) releases related to reserves for specific risks and uncertainties impacting vulnerable industries and regions, partially offset by increases in transfer risk associated with exposures outside of the U.S., driven by safety and soundness considerations under U.S. banking law.

Included in the allowance for loan and lease losses are qualitative reserves to cover losses that are expected but, in the Corporation's assessment, may not be adequately reflected in the quantitative methods or the economic assumptions described above.

comparisons.comparison: While Citi discusses the qualitative components of its ACL, Goldman Sachs (GS) disclosure focuses on the net change in the total allowance for credit losses. Both address the allowance for credit losses, but GS focuses on the net financial movement driven by macroeconomic factors, while Citi focuses on the qualitative judgment components.
